summary: Mostly quiet for holdings, with three items that matter. SAM (bought 11-17) named COO Phil Hodges CEO, effective 11-23, succeeding founder Jim Koch, which matches its 11-19 8-K 5.02. Baird downgraded FAST to Neutral ($56 PT), the name the PM already lists as the next sell candidate. A CRFB report alleges heavy metals in baby food sold at Kroger and Harris Teeter. No holding reports within 5 trading days: WMT reported 11-19 per its 8-K 2.02, and KR's company-confirmed 12-03 call enters the window around 11-25. Outside the book, ADSK and BBY have estimated prints on 11-24, 2 trading days out, and CVS now faces a proposed CMS Medicare Advantage audit rule (CMS-6098-P), a step past the earlier reports.

notable.headline: The Boston Beer Company Names Phil Hodges President and Chief Executive Officer (11-19, 23:02Z; 8-K 5.02/9.01 filed 11-19)
notable.read: A founder-CEO handover on a name bought 11-17, effective 11-23. The successor is the current COO, so this is an internal, planned-looking succession. That is the benign kind of 5.02, but the stored thesis was written before it was known. The headline does not say what role Koch keeps, and the filing is unread, so that is the open question. Separately, the 11-13 8-K 8.01 ages out after today unread. It closes by expiry, as BLBD's and FTDR's 5.02s did.

notable.headline: Baird Downgrades Fastenal to Neutral ($56 PT) (11-20)
notable.read: This is the first rating cut on FAST in my memory window. It lands on the name the PM restated on 11-19 as the next sell candidate (its 'marginal hold if XLI keeps lagging' condition is met). The downgrade is sell-side opinion, not an 8-K event, and it trips no measurable clause. It adds to the case the Proposer owes a trim/sale proposal or a hold verdict on (L8). The input doesn't show FAST's price, so I can't say how far $56 is from the market.

notable.headline: Report Alleges Presence of Toxic Heavy Metals in Baby Food Sold by Kroger and Harris Teeter (11-19)
notable.read: A new kind of negative for a held name: a CRFB investigation alleging baby food above FDA lead levels was sold despite new state laws. There is no recall, agency action or lawsuit in the input, so this is reputational and headline risk for now. It is not the cyber item KR's stored clause watches. It lands eight sessions before the 12-03 call, after three supportive initiations and PT raises (Goldman, Evercore, Stifel).

notable.headline: CVS Health Mentioned in Context of Proposed CMS 'CRUSH' Rule (11-20)
notable.read: The thread continues and escalates. It began with sell-side cuts (from 11-10), then Warren's breakup call (11-18), then a reimbursement report that knocked the shares (11-18). Now CMS has formally proposed MA audit recoveries back to 2018. That is an agency action on the economics of the Aetna arm, though only at the proposal stage. Not held. Anyone proposing CVS is underwriting this rule.
